item.title: NEW: Russian APT28 Breaches NATO Defense and Law Enforcement Entities
item.description:
Headline: Russian APT28 Breaches NATO Defense and Law Enforcement Entities

Summary:
The Russian-linked threat actor APT28 has been identified as the perpetrator of a sophisticated cyber-espionage campaign that successfully compromised a naval shipbuilder, a military aircraft engine manufacturer, and a law enforcement agency within two European NATO member states. The campaign, active from July to September 2026, utilized a backdoor known as HOOKEDGE and a previously undocumented reflective loader to execute payloads in memory, evading detection while stealing credential material and establishing persistent access via SSH tunnels.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Actor, Cyberattack, Data Breach

Meta Description: Russian-linked threat actor APT28 (Fancy Bear) compromised a naval shipbuilder, aircraft engine manufacturer, and law enforcement agency in two NATO countries.

item.title: NEW: Siemens Software Center Flaw (CVE-2026-110936) Actively Exploited
item.description:
Headline: Siemens Software Center Flaw (CVE-2026-110936) Actively Exploited

Summary:
Siemens has confirmed the active exploitation of a high-severity DLL side-loading vulnerability, CVE-2026-110936, in its Siemens Software Center (SSC) application. The flaw, rated 8.4 on the CVSS v4.0 scale, is being leveraged by the 'ClickFix' malware campaign. Attackers trick users into running a malicious installer that bundles a legitimate, older version of SSC with a malicious DLL, leading to arbitrary code execution. Siemens has released an update and urges customers to apply it.

Severity: High

Categories: Vulnerability, Industrial Control Systems, Malware

Meta Description: Attackers are actively exploiting a high-severity DLL side-loading vulnerability, CVE-2026-110936, in Siemens Software Center to deploy remote access trojans.

item.title: NEW: ConnectWise Shuts Down Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack
item.description:
Headline: ConnectWise Shuts Down Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack

Summary:
IT software provider ConnectWise has suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services following a significant supply-chain attack. The incident involved a compromised application credential for its multitenant OAuth application, which threat actors used to gain unauthorized, high-privilege access to the Microsoft 365 environments of its Managed Service Provider (MSP) partners and their customers. The attack bypassed user-based MFA, leading ConnectWise to take services offline and reset credentials.

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Cloud Security, Data Breach

item.title: NEW: Ransomware Gangs Exploit PAN-OS Auth Bypass to Infiltrate Networks
item.description:
Headline: Ransomware Gangs Exploit PAN-OS Auth Bypass to Infiltrate Networks

Summary:
Ransomware operators, including the groups known as Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (Inc), are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-0257, in Palo Alto Networks' PAN-OS software. This flaw in the GlobalProtect feature allows attackers to gain initial access and establish VPN sessions without valid credentials, bypassing multi-factor authentication. Security researchers at Unit 42 have observed advanced post-exploitation TTPs where attackers pivot from the compromised VPN gateway to the vCenter management appliance. From there, they disable security settings on ESXi hypervisors and use custom tooling to perform offline credential dumping against a domain controller's virtual disk (VMDK), a technique that evades typical EDR and in-guest security controls. Organizations are strongly urged to apply patches immediately.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Ransomware, Threat Actor

Article Type: Advisory

Reading Time: 4 minutes

Meta Description: Ransomware operators, including Qilin and Inc, are exploiting PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 to bypass MFA and gain network access. Patch now.

Summary:

The incident, which affected 1.4% of its Console users, resulted from unauthorized access to a legacy system. Attackers used the stolen keys in a 'distillation attack,' running up significant fraudulent charges on user accounts to likely train their own AI models. OpenCode has notified affected users and advised them to revoke and replace the compromised keys.

item.title: UPDATE: China-Linked Group Exploits BeyondTrust Zero-Day in Espionage Attacks
item.description:
Headline: China-Linked Group Exploits BeyondTrust Zero-Day in Espionage Attacks

Summary:
A China-linked cyber espionage group known as Armory Castle (UNC5221) has been exploiting a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-102764, in BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances. The flaw, with a CVSS score of 9.3, allows unauthenticated attackers to gain root-level control. The campaign, which began in late August 2026, involved deploying custom malware like the SAWFLY web shell and BARECLAW tunneler to achieve persistence, escalate privileges, and exfiltrate credentials from the device's secrets database. The attackers also wiped logs to cover their tracks. BeyondTrust has released patches and urges self-hosted customers to update immediately, rebuild compromised appliances from clean images, and rotate all associated credentials. The campaign targeted legal, technology, and government sectors, consistent with intelligence collection motives.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Threat Actor, Cyberattack

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: A China-linked cyber espionage group is exploiting a critical zero-day (CVE-2026-102764) in BeyondTrust Remote Support to gain root control and steal data.

Article Slug: china-linked-hackers-exploit-beyondtrust-zero-day-in-espionage-campaign
